title: An Artificial Intelligence Characterised Functional Ingredient, Derived from Rice, Inhibits TNF-α and Significantly Improves Physical Strength in an Inflammaging Population.
summary: An ensemble of ten neural networks predicted anti-inflammatory rice peptides, which were identified in a rice peptide hydrolysate and tested in vitro. A 12-week pilot randomized 40 older adults (30 rice NPN, 10 placebo); its primary digestive-discomfort endpoint was not met, while secondary physical-performance and biomarker outcomes favored treatment. Small sample, compliance/timing confounding, and the ingredient-versus-isolated-peptide distinction limit inference.
ai_technology: Trained neural-network ensemble for peptide bioactivity prediction

evidence.tested: Eight predicted peptides were synthesized; seven reduced TNF-α secretion in stimulated THP-1 assays. A 12-week pilot randomized 40 older adults (rice NPN 30, placebo 10). The digestive-discomfort primary endpoint was not met; secondary chair-stand/SPPB results favored treatment. Figure captions report at least 27/10 and 28/10 analyzed for those outcomes, respectively.
evidence.unknown: The pilot was small and randomized 30:10; the primary subjective endpoint was not met, and authors noted compliance and Christmas-period measurement as confounders. The clinical intervention was a rice peptide hydrolysate, so effects cannot be assigned to individual AI-predicted peptides. Clinical efficacy and generalizability need confirmation.
evidence.ai_role: A ten-model neural-network ensemble predicted anti-inflammatory peptides from food proteomes and helped characterize peptides detected in rice NPN; peptide and ingredient effects were then tested by mass spectrometry, cell assays, and a human pilot. The AI prediction itself did not establish clinical effect.

source_review.scope: Publisher Methods on peptide prediction and pilot design; peptide Results, human Results and outcome-specific figure-caption denominators.
